Team strategy plan:

We agree to maximize team profit. Current public info: we know our valuation is 57; others' valuations are unknown.

Plan for Round 1:
- All three (us, bidder_2, bidder_3) will submit the minimum bid of 10, ensuring we all participate and guarantee a chance to win.
- If we win, our profit = 57 - 10 = 47. If we don't win, we get 0.
- If any of the other two (the remaining of bidder_2/bidder_3) bid higher than 10, we will need to reassess next round based on public results.
- We will maintain this minimum-bid posture unless a round of results reveals something more profitable (e.g., higher valuations outbid us and we lose).

Team bidding note:

We will not announce our intended bid in this round yet. We want to observe public results and adapt. Keep the minimum bid (10) as our default if needed. We will call announce_bid when ready to bid in execution phase.

Team coordination for Round 2:

All three (bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3) will submit a bid of 10 credits each.

Rationale:
- Minimum allowed bid, so profit cost if winning is minimized (profit = valuation - 10).
- If all three bid 10, the winner is the highest valuation among the three, giving expected profit E[max(valuation)] - 10.
- This is optimal under the first-price auction structure with a minimum bid.

We will observe public results after each auction and adapt strategy if needed (e.g., if valuations all fall below a threshold, or if a specific high-value player wins unexpectedly).

Team coordination for Round 2 (bidder_2):

- All three (bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3) will submit 10 credits as the minimum bid.
- Rationale: minimizes the profit-cost per potential win (valuation - 10), ensuring we all participate.
- We will wait for public results to assess the round and refine strategy in subsequent rounds.

TEAM-LEVEL STRATEGY FOR ROUND 2:

Current state: I (bidder_1) valuation = 96. Total profit so far = 0.0. Previous round (Round 1) had all bids at minimum 10 with winner bidder_3, profit 0 for all.

Team plan for Round 2 (bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3 all together):

- All three submit the minimum bid of 10 credits.
- Rationale: This is the minimum allowed bid. It ensures all three continue to participate. Since everyone bids at least 10, the winner is simply the highest-valuation player among the three, and the winning profit = max(valuation) - 10. Bidding higher would increase the profit cost if we win, and since we cannot see others' valuations, higher bids cannot improve our probability of winning (in a first-price auction, the highest-valuation player wins regardless of bid, as long as we are not bid above theirs). The minimum bid maximizes our probability of being the highest-valuation player and is therefore optimal for the team's first-round profit in the upcoming round.

- We will observe public results after this auction and adapt in subsequent rounds (e.g., if we learn that our valuation is among the highest, we may reconsider in later rounds when more rounds remain).

This keeps the team in play and preserves all accumulated information for future adaptation.

Team coordination for Round 3: All three (bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3) will submit the minimum bid of 10 credits.

Rationale: We do not know the valuations of the other two bidders for this round, so bidding minimum minimizes the profit cost if we win and maximizes our chance of sharing a tie which is broken at random. Previous rounds showed the team winning with lower bids when valuations were high; here we stick with minimum to stay safe and adapt based on public results.

We will observe public results and adjust in Round 4 if more information is available.

All three submit minimum bid of 10 credits. We will observe auction results publicly and adapt next round. Combined strategy remains: minimum bid when valuations are uncertain, higher bids only if clear value emerges and we can confidently win.

Awaiting Round 3 results.

Round 4 plan: All three (bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3) will submit the minimum bid of 10 credits. Rationale: This guarantees all three participate, and when we win our profit is valuation - 10, which is higher than any higher bid. If we lose, profit is 0. Given no information that others will bid above minimum, this maximizes expected team profit. We will submit 10 in the execution phase.

Round 5 Planning: I (bidder_2) will bid 50 credits.

Reasoning:
- Previous rounds all had bids at minimum 10; past data suggests others bid 10 again
- If user bids 10 and ties (others bid 10): win prob 1/3, profit 114 → EV ~38
- If user bids 50 and others bid 10: guaranteed win at profit 74
- Bidding 50 sacrifices some upside but significantly increases guaranteed-win probability
- This is a team-agreed adaptation from the flat 10-bid strategy

Bid: 50

Next step: After execution phase, I (bidder_2) will observe public results. Based on that, I will decide whether to:
- Rebid 10 (fallback to flat minimum strategy) if this round didn't win, or
- Maintain higher bid if confident

I will post a message here with the outcome of auction 5.

ROUND 5 PLANNING: Team coordination for Round 5.

I (bidder_3) will bid 10 credits (minimum bid).

Rationale:
- All previous rounds used minimum bids (10), maintaining participation.
- Bidding minimum maximizes profit cost if I win (137 - 10 = 127) and minimizes the probability of being forced to bid above my valuation.
- If I win, my profit = 127. If I don't win, profit = 0.
- This is consistent with the team's low-bid strategy for rounds 1-4.
- We will observe public results and adapt next round if needed.

Final action: submit minimum bid of 10.

Round 6 planning for bidder_3 (team of bidder_1, bidder_2, bidder_3):

My valuation: 131 credits. Previous round (Round 5) had all bids at 10/50/50 with bidder_1 winning at 50 (profit 0).

Strategy: Submit minimum bid of 10 credits.

Rationale:
- Following the team's consistent minimum-bid strategy from Rounds 1-4.
- If I win at 10, my profit = 131 - 10 = 121 credits (high value).
- If I lose, profit = 0.
- Risk: if opponents bid > 10, I could be outbid. But given prior rounds show bids of 10 and 50, and my valuation is the highest known (131), staying at minimum maximizes the chance of surviving and potentially sharing a win.
- Alternative (bid 131) guarantees a win only if no one has higher valuation, but profit would be 0 in that case (bad).
- Team total profit so far: 167.0. Maximizing per-round wins improves this.

I will submit bid of 10 in the execution phase.

- Higher bids would reduce the team's payout in case of a win and offer no advantage in winning probability (your win condition is tied to having the highest valuation, independent of your bid, as long as you are not bid above the highest opponent).
- This aligns with the team's minimum-bid strategy from Rounds 1-4 and avoids the aggressive bid strategy used by bidder_2 in Round 5.
- Current public info: bidder_1 valuation 70, others' valuations unknown. No information suggests a deviation is advantageous.
